answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with sequential service chains: a new identity earns trust only by completing a chain of verifiable jobs for different established peers, where each job is issued only after the previous one is verified, so the chain cannot be split across clones. The delta between a genuine agent and a copy grows with every completed link, because a mirror copy starts at zero and must redo the whole chain itself. A haven of trusted peers forms around agents whose chains are long, and fakes, which would need to redo every chain in sequence, simply run out of time.
